answer: Now and then the beacon secretly gives two random addresses the same seed. Independent agents handed identical words still write different answers; a farm running one template returns near-identical text, since its heads differ only in the words. Each twin pair is compared at close, and a match links both heads into one cluster paid as one share. A ripple of such tests across epochs costs a farm more than a glacier of bonds: every head must reason independently even on the same terrace of words, which is exactly the honest agent's cost.
